note: Closed taxonomy. A finding may only be minted for a check_id listed here. mechanism maps to the Round-2 appendix nodes (A=crawl access, B=retrieval-time sourcing, C=machine reading, D=corroboration/identity, E=personalization/context, F=non-text payload).

checks.title: AI assistant crawlers are blocked in robots.txt
checks.description: robots.txt Disallows one or more major AI retrieval user-agents, so assistants cannot fetch the site at answer time.

checks.title: Site-wide noindex
checks.description: A noindex directive (meta or X-Robots-Tag) applies site-wide, removing pages from indexes.

checks.title: A whole content class is noindex/blocked
checks.description: An entire content template class is excluded from indexing or crawling.

checks.title: No usable sitemap
checks.description: No XML sitemap was found or it is empty/incoherent, hindering discovery of deep pages.

checks.title: robots.txt is unreachable (server error)
checks.description: robots.txt returns a 5xx/timeout; some crawlers treat an errored robots.txt as disallow-all.

checks.title: No robots.txt present
checks.description: Informational: no robots.txt served; permitted and means crawlers may access everything.

checks.title: robots.txt blocks all crawlers
checks.description: User-agent: * with Disallow: / blocks every compliant crawler from the whole site.

checks.title: This audit's user-agent is disallowed
checks.description: Informational: our crawler is disallowed; results reflect only what was permitted.

checks.title: Sitemap present but invalid
checks.description: A sitemap was served but is not well-formed XML or has an unexpected root element.

checks.title: Canonical URL points to an error page
checks.description: A page's canonical target returns 4xx/5xx, which can drop the page from indexes.

checks.title: Homepage returns an error status
checks.description: The entry point returns 4xx/5xx; the whole site is effectively invisible.

checks.title: Pages return server errors (5xx)
checks.description: Crawled pages return 5xx server errors.

checks.title: Redirect loop detected
checks.description: URLs enter a redirect loop or exceed the redirect limit; content is never reached.

checks.title: Long redirect chains
checks.description: URLs redirect several times before resolving, wasting crawl budget.

checks.title: Broken internal links
checks.description: Internal HTML link targets return confirmed 404, 410, or 5xx when fetched. A 403/401 is access-blocked, not automatically a broken page.

checks.title: Orphan-like pages
checks.description: Pages appear in the sitemap but have no internal links pointing to them.

checks.title: Content buried deep from the homepage
checks.description: Multiple pages are many clicks from the homepage and crawled less reliably.

checks.title: Important page(s) set to noindex
checks.description: The homepage or a key section carries a noindex directive.

checks.title: Important pages not reachable via internal links
checks.description: Key pages exist in the sitemap but have no internal links to reach them.

checks.title: Potential crawl trap
checks.description: Repeating path segments or session parameters can trap crawlers in an unbounded URL space.

checks.title: Inconsistent URL forms in internal links
checks.description: Informational: internal links use inconsistent URL forms, increasing duplicate crawling.

checks.title: Duplicate URL variants without a single canonical
checks.description: The same content is served at multiple URL variants that do not agree on one canonical URL.

checks.title: Pagination discoverability issue
checks.description: Paginated pages link (rel=next) to an unreachable or noindex page.

checks.title: Crawl budget risk from parameterized URLs
checks.description: A large share of internal links carry many parameters/session ids, exploding the crawl space.

checks.title: Inconsistent or self-conflicting canonical tags
checks.description: Canonical tags form loops, point at error URLs, or point at a clearly unrelated origin. A sibling-subdomain canonical is a review signal, not an automatic defect.

checks.title: Primary content only exists after JavaScript
checks.description: Raw HTML lacks the page's primary facts that appear only after client-side rendering; no-JS crawlers store an empty page.

checks.title: A content class has a large render gap
checks.description: A template class shows a large difference between raw-HTML text and rendered text for primary facts.

checks.title: Structured data is injected only after hydration
checks.description: JSON-LD is absent from raw HTML and present only in the rendered DOM, so no-JS fetchers miss it.

checks.title: Initial HTML is an empty app shell
checks.description: The raw HTTP response is an empty mount node with scripts; all content appears only after JavaScript, so no-JS fetchers store a blank page.

checks.title: Heading outline exists only after JavaScript
checks.description: The raw HTML has body text but the h1..h3 outline is injected by JavaScript, degrading machine parsing of the page structure.

checks.title: Material content is hidden from the accessibility tree
checks.description: A large share of the page's text sits in elements hidden behind interactions or removed from the accessibility tree, so assistants reading the exposed DOM miss it.

checks.title: Script-heavy page (content still present in raw HTML)
checks.description: Informational: the page loads many scripts but its content is already in the raw HTML; a performance note, not an accessibility defect.

checks.title: Meaningful text is represented only as images
checks.description: The page carries its meaningful text inside images rather than as HTML text, so machines cannot extract or quote it without OCR.

checks.title: Primary content is painted into <canvas>
checks.description: Primary content is rendered into a canvas element that exposes no text nodes; machines see an opaque bitmap.

checks.title: Key facts are locked in images/PDF
checks.description: Differentiating facts exist only inside images, canvas, or PDFs and not as extractable HTML text.

checks.title: Informational images lack alt text
checks.description: Images carrying information have empty or missing alt/figcaption, so extractors cannot read them.

checks.title: No quotable one-sentence value proposition
checks.description: No single plain-text sentence states what the brand is/does in a form an assistant can quote.

checks.title: Important fact stated only with a vague qualifier
checks.description: A fact category (pricing/hours/location) is referenced only with a vague phrase and no concrete value, so it cannot be extracted or quoted.

checks.title: Contradictory values for the same fact
checks.description: The structured data and the visible text disagree on the value of a fact (e.g. price), so an assistant may quote a wrong value.

checks.title: Fact not attributable to the correct entity
checks.description: A concrete fact (e.g. a product price) is shown without structured data tying it to a named entity, so it cannot be attributed correctly.

checks.title: Fact available only after interaction
checks.description: A fact category (FAQ/specs/policies) exists only inside hidden, interaction-gated DOM, so it is absent from the initial readable text.

checks.title: Structured data is present but invalid
checks.description: JSON-LD/microdata is present but fails schema.org validity (missing required properties or mismatched content).

checks.title: Brand entity is ambiguous / undisambiguated
checks.description: The brand name collides with other prominent entities and the site provides no disambiguators (sameAs, legal name, category).

checks.title: sameAs links missing or unresolvable
checks.description: Organization.sameAs is absent or points to dead/irrelevant profiles, weakening entity grounding.

checks.title: Malformed JSON-LD block
checks.description: A script[type=application/ld+json] block contains invalid JSON, so the entity it describes is invisible to machines.

checks.title: Unrecognized or inappropriate schema.org type
checks.description: An entity declares a @type that is not a valid schema.org class (typo/invented), so consumers ignore it.

checks.title: Contradictory structured data
checks.description: Structured data is internally inconsistent (e.g. dateModified before datePublished, or one @id reused across types).

checks.title: Structured data disagrees with visible content
checks.description: A schema value (name/price) is absent from or contradicts the visible page, so machines may quote a stale/wrong fact.

checks.title: Duplicate/conflicting primary entities
checks.description: Multiple distinct primary Organization entities exist, so machines cannot decide which entity owns the site.

checks.title: Entities present but not linked into a graph
checks.description: Product/page entities do not reference the Organization/Brand entity, so facts cannot be attributed to the company.

checks.title: Entity url inconsistent with page host
checks.description: An entity's url/@id points at a different host than the page it is served on, risking misattribution to another domain.

checks.title: Dated content is systematically stale
checks.description: dateModified/lastmod/latest-post signals indicate key content has not been updated in a long time.

checks.title: A key claim conflicts with independent sources
checks.description: A specific on-site claim contradicts corroborating independent sources (Wikidata/sameAs), inviting distrust.

checks.title: The site contradicts itself on a key fact
checks.description: A high-value claim (founding year, leadership, operating status) is stated with conflicting values across the site.

checks.title: Unusually strong claim with no support
checks.description: A superlative/absolute marketing claim is made with no attribution, citation, ranking source, or verifiable detail.

checks.title: A blocking interstitial precedes content
checks.description: A full-content-blocking overlay/modal appears before the visitor can see the page's value.

checks.title: Weak above-the-fold orientation
checks.description: A first-time visitor cannot answer what this is / for whom / what next from above-the-fold text and navigation.

checks.title: Missing information architecture signals
checks.description: No usable navigation, breadcrumbs, or site search to help visitors move through the site.

checks.title: Orientation content hidden behind interaction
checks.description: The entry page's main heading/value proposition exists only inside hidden or interaction-gated DOM, so it is absent from what a visitor first sees.

checks.title: Unexplained jargon in navigation
checks.description: Navigation uses unexpanded acronyms or terms that never appear defined on the site, which can confuse first-time visitors.

checks.title: Ambiguous or empty navigation links
checks.description: Links have empty or non-descriptive text (no aria-label), so visitors and assistants cannot tell where they lead.

checks.title: Inconsistent naming for the same destination
checks.description: The same destination is labelled differently across the primary navigation, breaking the visitor's mental map of the site.

checks.title: Dead-end page with no next step
checks.description: A page offers no navigation, no onward content links, and no call-to-action, leaving the visitor with nowhere to go.

checks.title: Key information not reachable from the home page
checks.description: Product, pricing, or contact pages exist but are not linked from the home page, adding friction before important information.

checks.title: Missing or zoom-blocking mobile viewport
checks.description: Pages lack a viewport meta tag or disable pinch-zoom, degrading mobile usability where it is reliably detectable.
